items.title: Caufield, Newhook each score twice in Canadiens’ win over Stars
items.body: DALLAS — Cole Caufield and Alex Newhook scored two goals each as the Montreal Canadiens beat the Dallas Stars 5-2 on Thursday night. Jakub Dobes made 17 saves in his first win since opening night as the Canadiens won their fourth consecutive game, all in Central Division rinks. Phillip Danault had an empty-net goal and an assist. Wyatt Johnston had a goal and an assist and Jamie Benn also scored for the Stars, who had won five straight before Tuesday’s 5-1 home loss to New Jersey. Jake Oettinger, who went into play third in the NHL with a 1.43 goals-against average, allowed a season-most four goals on 20 shots. Caufield opened the scoring with a one-timer 7:24 in. Only 27 seconds after Newhook broke a 1-1 tie late in the first period, Caufield stuffed in a puck that crossed behind Oettinger to give Montreal the lead for good. Newhook made it 4-1 early in the second period six seconds after Dallas’ top-ranked penalty kill notched the 25th of 27 consecutive kills scoring on a ricochet off the boards behind the net that Oettinger never saw. The Canadiens are 4-0 without captain Nick Suzuki, who was lost for two-to-four weeks on Oct. 20 with an upper-body injury. Dobes played instead of standout rookie Jacob Fowler, who has won his last six starts including Montreal’ three previous games. Dobes had allowed 20 goals in his four previous outings, going 0-2-2. In his previous start against Dallas early last season, Dobes was pulled after allowing five goals on 13 shots in a 7-0 loss. Montreal’s Noah Dobson and Dallas’ Mikko Rantanen (who turned 30 on Thursday) had two assists. Dallas is 3-2-0 with one game left in a season-long six-game homestand.

items.body: Interim GM 'disappointed' by forward, former captain's decision Dylan Larkin was suspended by the Detroit Red Wings on Thursday and has likely played his last game with the team. The forward, who requested a trade in the offseason, will be held out of the lineup without pay until a trade is worked out, interim general manager Shawn Horcoff said in a statement. "Dylan Larkin has informed us that he will no longer play for the Detroit Red Wings," the statement said. "We are disappointed by his decision, particularly given his obligations to the organization and his teammates. We have therefore suspended Dylan without pay. "We will continue to explore trade opportunities involving Dylan. In addition to needing his approval, any trade must also be in the best interest of the Detroit Red Wings and support the organization's long-term goals. "I want to thank and commend our coaches and players for their continued focus, and being committed to competing every day." The announcement from Horcoff came a few hours after coach Todd McLellan announced Larkin would not play against the Chicago Blackhawks at Little Caesars Arena on Thursday. Prior to the game, a 4-1 win for the Red Wings, Horcoff met with the media and reiterated the points made in his statement. "We received a call from Dylan’s agent today just saying that Dylan wasn’t going to be coming to the rink and no longer wanted to be a part of the Red Wings," Horcoff said. "From Day 1, I’ve worked extensively, exhaustively, with CAA to find a solution for Dylan. items.title: Cooley completes hat trick against hometown team with second left, Mammoth stun Penguins in OT
items.body: PITTSBURGH — Logan Cooley completed a hat trick against his hometown team with a second left, Mikhail Sergachev scored at 3:27 of overtime and the Utah Mammoth stunned the Pittsburgh Penguins 4-3 on Thursday night. After Ben Kindel put Pittsburgh ahead 3-2 with 25 seconds left, Cooley — playing his third NHL game in Pittsburgh — batted the puck in from the left side of the net for sixth goal in four games and seventh of the season. Cooley became the third Pittsburgh native with a hat trick against the Penguins, joining Brandon Saad and R.J. Umberger. At age 5, Cooley took part in Sidney Crosby’s first Little Penguins Learn to Play Hockey program. Cooley scored for the first time in seven games against Pittsburgh. He had two first-period goals to give the Mammoth an early 2-0 lead, and scored in the third for his third career hat trick. In overtime, Sergachev beat Arturs Silovs off a rebound in front. Sebastian Cossa stopped 31 shots for the Mammoth, who have won three of their last five games overall. Utah is 5-0-0 after a loss and 8-0-0 when leading after two periods. Rickard Rakell had a short-handed goal, and Erik Karlsson also scored for Pittsburgh. Silovs made 30 saves.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Mandatory Credit: Wendell Cruz-Imagn Images The New York Islanders announced that defenseman Ryan Pulock will not return to Thursday’s game against the Minnesota Wild due to an upper-body injury. Pulock sustained the injury early in the first period of the game, only playing in two shifts before he exited the match. It’s unclear what exactly caused the injury, but the most likely incident was when he was battling along the boards with Yakov Trenin, as he skated gingerly after the fact. He went to the dressing room after and did not return, with the team confirming his absence at the start of the second period. Pulock played just 51 seconds of ice time in those two shifts, with only a hit taken on his stat line before exiting the game. The Islanders were already down 1-0 at the time of his early departure. There’s currently no other updates on Pulock, including the severity of the injury and how much time he’s expected to miss. Islanders head coach Pete DeBoer might give an update after the game, but since the Isles are at the end of a three-game road trip before returning home, it’s likely that a more specific update isn’t provided until a practice or morning skate on Long Island. items.title: Jets rally but fall to Lightning for seventh straight loss
items.body: TAMPA, Fla. — Pontus Holmberg set a career high with four points on a goal and three assists, Brandon Hagel and Anthony Cirelli each had a goal and two assists, and the Tampa Bay Lightning remain unbeaten at home with a 6-4 victory over the Winnipeg Jets on Thursday night. Brayden Point, John Carlson and Conor Geekie all scored for Tampa Bay. Andrei Vasilevskiy stopped 17 shots. The Lightning improved to 6-0 at home to tie a franchise record to start a season. Neil Pionk, playing his 600th game, scored twice. Kyle Connor and Dylan Samberg also scored for the Jets and Mark Scheifele had three assists. Stuart Skinner allowed five goals on 21 shots before being replaced by Nico Daws to start the third period. Daws finished with nine saves in his Winnipeg debut. Winnipeg is winless (0-5-2) in the past seven games, including three consecutive regulation losses since trading goaltender Connor Hellebuyck to New Jersey. After Point and Pionk traded goals in the first period, Tampa Bay pulled away in the second period with four goals, including three in the final 4:04. Geekie backhanded in a pass from Dominic James at 9:43 before Cirelli scored a power-play goal at 15:56, getting his stick on a cross-crease pass from Holmberg. Carlson made it 4-1 at 18:07 as he one-timed Holmberg's pass from the left faceoff dot. Hagel finished off the period with a tap-in from Cirelli at the back post with 56 seconds left in the period. Winnipeg scored two goals less than two minutes apart in the third to cut into the lead. Perfetti fed Samberg for a one-handed redirect at 7:00 while Pionk scored his second at 8:50, with Dawson Mercer registering his first point with the Jets on the play. Connor scored with 2:49 left to make it a one-goal game.

He went on to notch 56 points in 2022-23, then scored 57 points in 69 games in each of the 2023-24 and 2024-25 campaigns. Across his career, Hughes has only appeared in five NHL matchups. items.body: Former captain was suspended after informing team he would no longer play for them DETROIT -- Dylan Larkin has sealed his legacy in his hometown. Whatever goodwill he had rebuilt is gone. The former captain left the Detroit Red Wings on Thursday, and they suspended him without pay. The only question now is when Detroit will trade him and what it will receive in return, but the crux of the problem remains: Larkin has requested a trade while limiting the market with his no-trade clause, hampering the Red Wings’ ability to make a deal that works for them. They cannot give away their No. 1 center just because he wants to leave. So, it’s difficult. “How long it takes, I’m not sure. items.body: The Nashville Predators inducted their former head coach and general manager into the Golden Hall before the team’s game against the Washington Capitals at Bridgestone Arena. Predators owner Bill Haslam, former general manager David Poile and team CEO Sean Henry joined Trotz on the ice for the ceremony. A special tribute video of Trotz’s career with Nashville aired on the arena video board. After the video, Poile presented the golden jacket to Trotz as “Barry! Barry!” chants rang from the crowd. “Thank you so much, thank you,” Trotz said. “I’ve been blessed to work with three wonderful organizations and two are here tonight. I’m honored and humbled to be inducted into the Golden Hall and stand beside Predator greats like David Poile, Shea Weber , Pekka Rinne , Terry Crisp, Peter Weber. It’s an honor.” Another tribute video aired before the newest Golden Hall member performed the ceremonial puck drop between Predators captain Roman Josi and Washington Capitals captain Alex Ovechkin . Before the game, Trotz exchanged gifts with Ovechkin, who is playing his final career game in Nashville . He coached Ovechkin and the Capitals from 2014-2018, leading them to their first Stanley Cup title in 2018. Ovechkin and Tom Wilson gifted their former coach a custom bottle of wine. Reuniting for the last time in Smashville 🤝 pic.twitter.com/CYvdYOQ4sX In 1997, Trotz was hired as the Predators’ first-ever head coach, leading the team for 15 seasons until 2014. From 2023-26, he served as the team’s general manager. Trotz is currently semi-retired and acts as an advisor to the franchise.

items.body: Register Login Hurricanes’ Taylor Hall Out Day-To-Day By Gabriel Foley | at October 29, 2026 7:10 pm Taylor Hall has fallen back out of the Carolina Hurricanes lineup with a day-to-day injury. The 34 year old sustained a new injury in Tuesday’s practice, unrelated to his upper-body injury sustained on October 13th, per ESPN’s Emily Kaplan . Hall has not played since his initial injury, though he was activated off of injured reserve on Monday . He went on to miss Tuesday’s game against the Boston Bruins, marking six consecutive absences for Hall. The Hurricanes offense is inevitably shorthanded without Hall in the lineup. His absence keeps Carolina from rolling out the trio of Hall, Logan Stankoven , and Jackson Blake – a unit that has outscored opponents 38-to-26 dating back to last season. They won the scoring battle three-to-one through the first eight games of this season. Individually, Hall has racked up five points in eight appearances. Half of that scoring came from back-to-back two-point performances on October 6th and 8th. The Hurricanes combined for 13 goals between those two games. Carolina has continued to find success despite Hall’s absence. They lead the NHL with a 10-2-2 record and rank third in scoring with 3.79 goals-per-game. Stankoven and Blake have been joined by Nikolaj Ehlers , forming a line that has four goals-for and no goals-against. Hall’s absence has also opened an opportunity for Nicolas Deslauriers , who should stick on the fourth-line until the former Hart Trophy winner is back to full health. Skyler Brind’Amour also made appearances during Hall’s initial stint on IR. He was assigned in a corresponding move to Hall’s activation and could return to the lineup as an extra option.

items.title: PWHL increases minimum salary and roster size for 2026-27
items.summary: The PWHL is increasing the minimum pay for players, while also taking away the “reserve player” status from team roster builds.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources The PWHL is increasing the minimum player salary from around $38,000 to $42,000 for the 2026-27 season and will raise it to $52,500 by the 2030-31 season, the league and the PWHL Players Association announced Thursday. The increased salaries headline a list of sweeping changes to pay and roster construction, including teams increasing to 24-player rosters for the upcoming campaign and abolishing the league’s “reserve player” status, which had players in full-commitment but only making $15,000 as a full-season stipend. “As the PWHL expands from eight to 12 teams, these changes reflect our shared commitment to creating more opportunities for players, strengthening the economic foundation of professional women’s hockey and supporting the league’s long-term growth,” the joint statement said. “The PWHL and PWHLPA remain committed to working collaboratively to advance player opportunities, compensation, and the continued growth of professional women’s hockey.” With the increase in roster sizes, 288 players will be under contract for the 2026-27 season across the league’s dozen teams, now split into two conferences of six for the first time. At the same time, teams can use a One-Game Standard Player Agreement mechanism to sign replacements in case of injuries or other hardships that hit the roster. While the season is not set to get underway until Dec. 5, competitive hockey has already dropped the puck, with pre-tournament international games in the lead-up to the first edition of the rescheduled fall IIHF Women’s World Championship , set to take place in Denmark from Nov. 6-16 as a precursor to the professional season in North America. As the Rays have done for years, Dubas locked up an unproven player with a big extension at a surprising price. Penguins head coach Dan Muse said to reporters Thursday morning that "everything's looking good" with Kindel, Evgeni Malkin and Egor Chinakhov, "so expecting them in." items.body: Register Login Snapshots: Shabanov, Lardis, 2027 Draft By Ethan Hetu | at October 29, 2026 2:33 pm While it’s still very early in the 2026-27 season, it’s not too early to begin looking at players who may be setting themselves up to earn a big pay raise in the summer. With the salary cap rising at a steep rate, promising individual performances can have even more weight as teams look to identify and pay players before those players can realize the full extent of their value on the open market. The Anaheim Ducks’ decision to pay Tristan Luneau , with less than 30 NHL games to his name, a $7.2MM AAV on a long-term contract extension serves as an illustration of this principle in action. One player who is lining himself up to earn a substantial pay raise is Minnesota Wild winger Max Shabanov . The 26-year-old former KHL star endured a difficult NHL rookie season with the New York Islanders in 2025-26, and New York ultimately non-tendered him after he scored just 18 points in 44 games. The Wild inked Shabanov to a one-year, $1.6MM deal, and he’ll be an RFA with arbitration rights over the summer. His early-season form suggests a major pay raise could be in store, as he’s found himself a regular role on Minnesota’s top power play unit and has produced nine points in his first 13 games with the Wild.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images A veteran pivot has hit the waiver wire. On Thursday, the Dallas Stars placed center Cameron Hughes on waivers. Hughes is now available to be claimed by the other 31 teams in the NHL. If he clears waivers, he’ll be eligible to be assigned to Dallas’ American Hockey League (AHL) affiliate Texas Stars. Hughes, 30, has yet to get into game action for the Stars this season after he suffered an upper-body injury during preseason. As a result, he began the year on injured reserve. items.title: Dylan Larkin to stay out of games until Red Wings complete trade
items.body: The Detroit Red Wings ' former captain will not play until a trade occurs, Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman reported on Thursday. The development follows head coach Todd McLellan's announcement that Larkin will not play against the Chicago Blackhawks on Thursday. McLellan said Detroit's interim general manager Shawn Horcoff would address the situation. Larkin, 30, requested a trade during the summer. He did report to the team, but was stripped of his captaincy. The three-time all-star, who has a no-trade clause, has reportedly expanded his trade list to 10 teams. Helene St. James of The Detroit Free Press has reported that Larkin's list now includes the Florida Panthers, Minnesota Wild, Vegas Golden Knights, Dallas Stars, Washington Capitals, Carolina Hurricanes, Utah Mammoth, Tampa Bay Lightning, New Jersey Devils and Colorado Avalanche. While former general manager Steve Yzerman fielded calls for Larkin, those talks stalled while the Red Wings searched for a new head of hockey operations once he was removed from his post on July 15. That search is ongoing but Horcoff was elevated to interim general manager in September and seemingly has the authority to complete a Larkin trade. One team notably not on Larkin's trade list is the Montreal Canadiens, even after Canadiens fans chanted "we want Larkin!" during a recent visit by the Red Wings. However, Red Wings assistant GM Kris Draper has watched the Canadiens live several times this season.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Tampa Bay Lightning are getting one of their top players back into their lineup, and his arrival could not be coming at a better time. Winger Brandon Hagel, who has not missed a game but had his status for this contest up in the air, will also play. Moser, Ryan McDonagh, John Carlson and Erik Cernak in the fold, the Lightning have been able to shelter Hedman and effectively manage his role in his age-35 season. Veteran forward Zemgus Girgensons will not play and is out on a day-to-day basis, and Tampa has plenty of depth defensively to spread minutes around on the back end. The Lightning, perennially one of the top teams in the Eastern Conference, have looked like such to start this season, but a dearth of games played compared to their Atlantic Division foes has them sitting in sixth in the division by points, though they’re second by points percentage. Despite the overall strong start, Tampa has dropped its past two games as the Jets come to town, so the Bolts will be looking to get right against a Winnipeg team that started the year out hot but has lost six straight games to plummet down the Central Division standings.

items.body: The Florida Panthers could be about a month away from nearing full forward health. Captain Aleksander Barkov and veteran winger Brad Marchand both resumed skating Thursday as they take a step toward a return from injury, head coach Paul Maurice told reporters . Barkov remains four weeks away from playing games while Marchand is three weeks out, Maurice added. The captain, who missed all of last season due to a right knee injury, went down in just his second game this season with a left knee injury that ultimately did not require surgery. His original timeline of six to eight weeks from the early October exit appears to still be intact. He’s supposed to be embarking on a career in law enforcement right about now. He’s been paying the bills working at a gun range. Instead, he’s staring down Alex Ovechkin’s one-timer, again and again and again, until ‘Ovi,’ the greatest goal scorer who ever lived, feels like he has it calibrated well enough for the day. Leslie has to avoid fanboying out too much. He has a job to do. He’s trying to keep Washington Capitals goaltenders Logan Thompson and Charlie Lindgren fresh. It’s scary facing the patented Ovechkin shot, which beats Leslie most of the time – it’s famous for a reason, he says – but he’s thrilled if he can block, deflect, even graze one of them. Day to day, he’s doing his best to stand in for an NHL goalie, getting in front of shots, trying not to make things too easy for the Capitals’ players. He thinks he’s merely part of the background, barely noticed. But not today, when Tom Wilson asks the coaching staff to pause the drill instruction for an announcement. Leslie is turning 25 today, and he stands on the ice, in full NHL-regulation gear, listening to the Capitals sing Happy Birthday to him. It’s surreal. Leslie is one of them now. Mathieu Joseph, Mattias Ekholm, Kasperi Kapanen and Alex Formenton had the goals for the Oilers (9-2-2). Connor McDavid and Ryan Nugent-Hopkins each had a pair of assists. Edmonton wrapped up its five-game road trip with a 3-1-1 record. The Flames (5-7-0) saw a four-game winning streak come to an end. Oilers: McDavid extended his season-starting points streak to all 13 games, adding two assists to give him a league-leading 36 points. He also extended his campaign-starting assists streak to 13 games, setting a new record by surpassing the likes of Sebastian Aho, Ken Linseman and Wayne Gretzky for the longest in NHL history. Edmonton made it 3-0 on the power play just 55 seconds into the third with a nice display of passing as McDavid sent it to Kapanen for his fourth. items.body: Register Login Nick Shore Signs Through End Of Season In Switzerland By Gabriel Foley | at October 28, 2026 6:57 pm Former Los Angeles Kings centerman Nick Shore has extended his tenure in Switzerland’s National League. The 34 year old originally signed a short-term contract with HC Lugano that was set to expire at the end of October. With that date approaching, he has formally signed through the end of the 2026-27 season. Shore is among Lugano’s top scorers, with 13 points in 14 league games with the club. A full-season contract will commit Shore to a full season in Switzerland’s top league, a setting he has already thrived in before. Shore won a National League championship with EV Zug in 2021. He scored 27 points in 22 games, then added eight points in 13 playoff matchups. That was his first season overseas, though he began the year in Slovakia’s top league with HK Dukla Trencin. Switzerland, and a championship, must have made a warm impression, as Shore went on to join HC Ambri-Piotta for the start of the 2022-23 season. He made another mid-season move that year, heading to HV71 in Sweden’s SHL. Shore stayed in the SHL – splitting his time between HV71 and Linkoping HC – until the end of the 2025-26 season. items.body: Register Login Capitals Activate Logan Thompson; Reassign Mitch Gibson By Brennan McClain | at October 28, 2026 3:58 pm After returning as a regular to practice yesterday, the Washington Capitals will return their starting netminder to the active roster. According to beat reporter Sammi Silber , the Capitals activated netminder Logan Thompson from the injured reserve and assigned Mitch Gibson to the AHL’s Hershey Bears. Thompson has been on Washington’s injured reserve with a lower-body ailment since their October 20th matchup against the Los Angeles Kings. Fortunately, the Capitals had only one game in the past week, limiting Thompson’s absence. Despite beating the Buffalo Sabres on Saturday, Washington likely wasn’t confident in Charlie Lindgren as the starter moving forward. The Capitals’ defense bailed him out for much of the game, limiting the Sabres to 21 shots on net through 63:42. Still, Lindgren stopped only 15 of those attempts, leading to a disappointing .857 SV% on the night. Now the Capitals can return to a netminder who has been on cruise control since joining the organization ahead of the 2024-25 campaign. This season, Thompson has earned a 4-3-0 record in seven starts with a .901 SV% and 2.90 GAA, including 1.9 Goals Saved Above Average. Throughout the past two years, Thompson has managed a dominant 62-27-12 record with a .911 SV% and 2.46 GAA, including two fourth-place finishes in Vezina Trophy voting. Meanwhile, Gibson returns to AHL Hershey without debuting in the NHL. He’s gotten off to a subpar start this season, splitting his first two appearances with an .881 SV% and 3.50 GAA.

items.body: Register Login Stars Reassign Dylan Hryckowian By Brennan McClain | at October 28, 2026 3:20 pm Forward Dylan Hryckowian ’s first call-up with the Dallas Stars will be short-lived. According to a team announcement , the Stars have returned Hryckowian to the AHL’s Texas Stars. Hryckowian, teammate Justin Hryckowian ’s younger brother, will return to the AHL after two games with Dallas. Unfortunately, Hryckowian went scoreless in both contests, with a -1 rating and averaged 9:00 of ice time per game. Still, he registered a solid 53.8% CorsiFor at even strength, albeit in limited action. Although he will likely return to the NHL in the near future, the Stars simply need additional depth elsewhere. Earlier this morning, head coach Glen Gulutzan confirmed that defenseman Kyle Capobianco got an MRI after suffering a leg injury in last night’s contest against the New Jersey Devils ( per NHL’s Robert Tiffin ). According to Tiffin, Gulutzan said, “ I don’t think it’s 6 to 8 weeks here, but I would say he’s gonna be out a week here, for sure. ” Already down to six defensemen on the active roster, Dallas needed to open up space to recall another defenseman. Veteran Kyle Burroughs is the likeliest candidate, since he’s one of the few blue liners on AHL Texas with NHL experience. Additionally, optimism is growing that Sam Steel will return to the lineup tomorrow, negating the need for additional forward depth. Steel has missed the Stars’ previous two contests due to an undisclosed injury. He has registered one goal and three points in 10 games this season.

items.body: Register Login Penguins Announce Multiple Roster Moves By Brennan McClain | at October 28, 2026 3:05 pm The Pittsburgh Penguins are returning one of their best free-agent acquisitions from a season ago. According to a team announcement , the Penguins activated forward Justin Brazeau from the injured reserve and placed Elmer Söderblom on it in a corresponding roster move. Pittsburgh has also assigned Avery Hayes and defenseman Chase Pietila to the AHL’s Wilkes-Barre/Scranton Penguins. Reassigning Hayes and Pietila opens the door for the Penguins to make a few more activations tomorrow. Based on practice over the past two days, optimism is growing that defenseman Samuel Girard (undisclosed) and forward Benjamin Kindel (vasovagal episode) could return for tomorrow’s contest against the Utah Mammoth. Brazeau has been recovering from a lower-body injury suffered in preseason. After missing 18 games last season, Brazeau has already missed Pittsburgh’s first 12 contests of the 2026-27 campaign. Still, if he’s anything like the player he was last year, he’ll provide the Penguins with an offensive jolt. The New Liskeard, ON, native signed a two-year, $3MM ($1.5MM AAV) contract with Pittsburgh ahead of the 2025-26 campaign. He fit in exceptionally well with the Penguins, scoring 17 goals and 34 points in 64 games with a +5 rating, averaging 12:39 of ice time. Brazeau typically played next to Anthony Mantha and Kindel on the Penguins’ third line. Unfortunately, Brazeau’s activation is paired with Söderblom’s new injury. Yesterday, Pittsburgh announced that Söderblom would miss the next few days with an upper-body injury. Fortunately, given their relatively long break between games, Söderblom will be eligible to return on Saturday, having missed only one game.

items.summary: Nikc Blankenburg, John Tavares, and Marshall Rifai are all considered week-to-week with injuries.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Sergei Belski-Imagn Images A heavy amount of injury news in The Six. On Wednesday, the Toronto Maple Leafs announced that forward Kirill Marchenko is considered week-to-week with a lower-body injury. On top of that, the Maple Leafs revealed that forward Dakota Joshua has been recalled from his conditioning loan to the team’s American Hockey League franchise, the Toronto Marlies. Marchenko suffered a lower-body injury during Monday night’s loss to the Calgary Flames . During the second period, the 26-year-old fell awkwardly into the boards after receiving a hit from Flames forward Yegor Sharangovich. Marchenko trudged off the ice in pain, walked down the tunnel to the Leafs’ dressing room and didn’t return to the contest. Marchenko has been a solid addition to Toronto’s lineup since the Original Six franchise received him in a preseason blockbuster trade with the Columbus Blue Jackets . In 14 games thus far, he has posted six goals and 14 points. While the Leafs had to give up a young Matthew Knies to make the deal happen, early returns are positive for the Russian winger. In 307 career regular-season NHL games, Marchenko has collected 108 goals and 222 points. The Leafs had updates on a couple of other players who are on the shelf. Defenseman Chris Tanev remains out of action with an upper-body injury, but is considered day-to-day after returning to practice. Forward John Tavares and defender Marshall Rifai are also week-to-week with lower-body injuries. Defenseman Nick Blankenburg, who was placed on injured reserve last week, remains week-to-week with a UBI as well. The Maple Leafs (7-5-2) look to get back in the win column on Wednesday night, when they visit the Seattle Kraken .

items.title: Oliver Moore looks for more growth after good response to healthy scratch
items.summary: In Oliver Moore’s 70th NHL game, the promising forward made an ill-advised pass in Chicago’s offensive zone that led to a tying goal for Montreal.
items.body: CHICAGO — In Oliver Moore 's 70th NHL game, the promising forward made an ill-advised pass in Chicago's offensive zone that led to a tying goal for Montreal. In Moore's 71st game, he was all over the ice in a big win for the Blackhawks. That's how it's going at the moment in Chicago, where the team's youngest players are still learning on the job. Moore was a healthy scratch for Sunday’s 3-2 loss to Florida, but he returned to the lineup Tuesday night and played quite well in a 2-1 victory over the Los Angeles Kings. “I didn’t expect anything less,” coach Jeff Blashill said. “He actually was playing good hockey. I felt it was a moment where him and our team needed to make sure we learn these lessons about not beating ourselves. But he’s played good hockey, so it’s not like he went through a stretch where he hadn’t been playing well. He stepped right back in and did a good job.” Moore, a first-round pick in the 2023 draft, is a key figure for Chicago as it tries to find the other side of years of rebuilding. The 21-year-old Minnesota native signed a $21.25 million, five-year contract in September. Losers of eight of their first 12 games, the Blackhawks are looking for more offence once again. They are averaging 2.17 goals, ranking No. 31 in the NHL going into Wednesday's action. They averaged just 2.56 goals last season. Moore has elite speed and athleticism, but he is still working on finishing his scoring opportunities. He has two goals and one assist in 11 games after he had five goals and 14 assists in 51 games all of last season. Facing Montreal on Friday, he tried to make a backhand pass from the corner to Ryan Greene in the middle. It was intercepted by Owen Beck, who started a rush that led to Jake Evans' tying score in the first period of the Canadiens' 4-1 win.

items.body: Register Login Senators Place Cameron Crotty On Waivers By Brennan McClain | at October 28, 2026 1:35 pm According to Sportsnet’s Elliotte Friedman , the Ottawa Senators have placed defenseman Cameron Crotty on waivers. The transaction strongly indicates that defenseman Thomas Chabot will return tomorrow evening against the Los Angeles Kings. Crotty, 27, has been in the Senators organization for the past two years. The Ottawa native was originally selected with the 82nd overall pick in the 2017 NHL Draft by the now-defunct Arizona Coyotes, and he spent his collegiate tenure with the Boston University Terriers. Playing under head coach Albie O’Connell , Crotty finished his NCAA career with 10 goals and 27 points in 102 games with a +11 rating. With all due respect to Crotty, he’s no more than a depth defender at this stage of his career. Largely an AHL talent since turning pro, Crotty has bounced from the Tucson Roadrunners to the Iowa Wild before landing with the Senators. His most productive years were with the Roadrunners when he scored four goals and 26 points in 119 combined games during the 2022-23 and 2023-24 seasons. In the NHL, Crotty has served as an injury replacement, typically only when the other injury replacement is injured. Debuting with the Coyotes in the 2023-24 season, Crotty has skated in 11 games since, registering one assist with a -1 rating, averaging 12:34 of ice time per game. Because of his lackluster resume, it’s likely that Crotty will pass through waivers unscathed. He’s expected to rejoin the AHL’s Belleville Senators once eligible.

Bystedt, 22, has four goals and eight points through eight games with the Barracuda to start the 2026-27 AHL regular season. The Sharks originally selected the six-foot-three, left-shot center in the first round (No. 27 overall) of the 2022 NHL Draft. The Sharks also recalled defenseman Libor Hajek on Wednesday while placing forwards Igor Chernyshov and Alex Wennberg on injured reserve. Additionally, the club assigned defenseman Luca Cagnoni to the Barracuda. The Sharks have lost three consecutive games and finally chose to recall Bystedt the day after they fell 2-0 to the Buffalo Sabres on home ice. Through 13 games this season, the Sharks sit just outside the Western Conference playoff picture with a 6-6-1 record and 13 points. After being drafted by the Sharks in 2022, Bystedt spent the subsequent two seasons with his hometown Swedish Hockey League club Linköping HC. He scored 15 goals and 37 points in 92 games over his two full campaigns with Linköping before arriving in North America in 2024. Beyond his club play, Bystedt also represented his native Sweden internationally at the 2023 and 2024 IIHF World Junior Championships, collecting seven goals and 14 points in 14 games across the two tournaments. Bystedt has spent parts of the past four seasons with the Barracuda and could make his NHL debut with the Sharks as soon as Thursday’s game against the Vancouver Canucks . He scored 22 goals and 60 points in 65 games with the Barracuda in 2025-26 and was named to the 2026 AHL All-Star Game. items.title: Maple Leafs provide injury updates for several players
items.summary: The Toronto Maple Leafs are up against it as the injury list continues to grow.
items.body: The Toronto Maple Leafs are up against it as the injury list continues to grow. The Leafs provided several updates on key players currently on the team's injured list on Wednesday, including a clearer timeline for star winger Kirill Marchenko . Marchenko, who exited Monday's 5-2 loss to the Calgary Flames with a lower-body injury, has been listed week-to-week. The 26-year-old was acquired by the Maple Leafs on the eve of the season from the Columbus Blue Jackets in exchange for Matthew Knies. He's producing at a point-per-game clip with his new team, registering 14 points (six goals, eight assists) in 13 games leading up to Monday. In brighter news, defenceman Chris Tanev has been upgraded to day-to-day. He's been out of the lineup since Oct. 10, when he suffered an upper-body injury against the Colorado Avalanche. He returned to Leafs practice on Monday, and on Wednesday was spotted without a no-contact sweater. Tanev has struggled to stay healthy over the past two seasons. He appeared in just 11 games last season due to multiple injuries and underwent season-ending core muscle surgery in March. So far this year, he has one assist in six games. Also listed on the team's injury report are Nick Blankenburg (week-to-week, upper-body), John Tavares (week-to-week, lower-body), Marshall Rifai (week-to-week, lower-body) and Dakota Joshua (recalled from conditioning loan with Marlies). The Leafs (7-5-2) return to action Wednesday as they visit the Seattle Kraken.

items.body: Register Login Blue Jackets Place Carson Soucy On Waivers By Brennan McClain | at October 28, 2026 1:23 pm After activating Dante Fabbro yesterday, the Columbus Blue Jackets are looking to shed some extra weight in their defensive corps. According to Aaron Portzline of The Athletic , the Blue Jackets have placed defenseman Carson Soucy on waivers. If he’s claimed, Soucy will join his fifth organization in three years. The Viking, Alberta, native began his NHL career in the 2017-18 season with the Minnesota Wild and was eventually drafted by the Seattle Kraken in the 2021 Expansion Draft. Soucy, 32, was solid in his two-year stint with the upstart Kraken. In the 2021-22 and 2022-23 seasons, Soucy scored 13 goals and 37 points in 142 games with a +25 rating, and an average of 16:55 of ice time per game. He also blocked 169 shots and delivered 261 hits during that stretch, finishing with a 51.4% CorsiFor and 90.5% on-ice SV% at even strength. Because of his strong play, Soucy earned his second multi-year contract, signing a three-year, $9.75MM ($3.25MM AAV) deal with the Vancouver Canucks as an unrestricted free agent. Unfortunately, injury troubles began immediately, and Soucy fell out of favor with Vancouver. The Canucks traded him to the New York Rangers the following season for a 2025 third-round selection. His play didn’t improve after a change of scenery. In 62 games with the Rangers, Soucy scored four goals and 11 points with a +6 rating, averaging nearly 17 minutes of ice time per game. items.title: Thomas Chabot nearing return as Senators place Cameron Crotty on waivers
items.summary: The Senators have placed defenceman Cameron Crotty on waivers Wednesday, making room for the potential return of Thomas Chabot ahead of Thursday’s game against the Los Angeles Kings.
items.body: Already off to a strong start this season, the Ottawa Senators are set to get a big piece back in the fold. The Senators placed defenceman Cameron Crotty on waivers Wednesday, making room for the potential return of Thomas Chabot ahead of Thursday's game against the Los Angeles Kings. Chabot has been out since suffering an upper-body injury against the Philadelphia Flyers on Oct. 18. However, he's been back practising with the Senators and shed his non-contact jersey at Monday's skate. The 29-year-old was named the 11th captain in Senators history ahead of the season (and became the first francophone to wear the 'C' in Ottawa), replacing Brady Tkachuk, who was traded to the Florida Panthers. Before suffering the injury, the Sainte-Marie, Que. native had tallied one goal and three assists while posting a plus-5 rating in the Senators' first nine games. Crotty, meanwhile, has played three games for the Senators this season without getting a point. His last appearance was on Oct. 15 against the New York Islanders. Selected by the Arizona Coyotes in the third round of the 2017 draft, the Ottawa native has one assist in 11 career NHL games, split between the Senators, Coyotes and Wild.

items.title: Matthew Schaefer impresses yet again with lengthy overtime
items.summary: Schaefer was on the ice for all five minutes of the extra frame in the Islanders’ shootout win over the Predators.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images One of the younger stars of the game continues to amaze. The New York Islanders and Nashville Predators had an exciting battle on Tuesday night, with the two teams going to overtime tied 3-3. The Islanders, desperate for the extra point, threw defenseman Matthew Schaefer out right off the hop and kept him there. The reigning Calder Trophy winner played the entire overtime period, which included a power play for the Isles. Despite not being able to find the winner in the extra frame, Schaefer’s team ended up coming away with the victory in a shootout. He ended up leading all skaters with 32:16 of ice time, an exceptional effort for a player many believe will carry the torch for years to come. On Wednesday’s edition of Daily Faceoff LIVE , Tyler Yaremchuk and Carter Hutton discuss Schaefer’s impressive effort in a victorious outcome. Tyler Yaremchuk: [In OT] They go back and forth for the first couple of minutes. Arm shoots up, delayed penalty. It was Forsberg who tripped Matthew Schaefer. The Islanders kind of got like 15-20 seconds to cycle the puck around on a delayed penalty, which I think kind of helped Schaefer catch his breath a little bit. Then, ahead of the power play, there was 2:14 left in overtime ahead of that power play. The Islanders called a timeout to get Schaefer rested and back on the ice. Pretty insane he was able to do that.
